references.text: Amos describes the same curse where vineyards will not yield fruit, as part of God's judgment on Israel.
Haggai mentions that people sow much but harvest little, and drink but are not satisfied—the same theme of futile labor as God's judgment.
Micah prophesies that the people shall plant but not reap, tread olives but not anoint themselves with oil—a parallel curse.
Joel describes how locusts and larvae destroy the crops, including the grapevines.
Isaiah describes that ten measures of vineyard will yield only one bat of wine—the same theme of failed viticulture as God's judgment.
Earlier in the same chapter, a similar curse is mentioned about planting a vineyard but not enjoying its fruit.
The Lord struck the crops with blight, mildew, and hail—similar destruction of crops as God's discipline.
